They therefore made the lake Maeotis, which receives the Tanaïs, and the Caspian Sea, which also they call a lake, one body of water, affirming that there was a subterraneous opening between both, and that one was part of the other. That it was not a different lake from the Maeotis, he conjectures from the circumstance of the Tanaïs discharging itself into it.
